name: W.A. spring-driven verge watch
description: A watch dated 1571 has a spring-driven movement with a verge escapement and balance; the museum notes that the verge and balance may be replacements.

impact.note: One surviving dated watch, possibly with replaced parts, witnessing an existing craft; nothing later is known to rest on this object.

date.basis: The catalogue dates the watch by the year engraved on its dial; possible replacement components are not independently dated to 1571.

events.statement: The Metropolitan Museum dates the W.A. watch to 1571 and describes its present spring-driven verge and balance movement.
events.place_note: Attributed to Antwerp or possibly Ghent, in the region now Belgium.

evidence.locator: Object details, movement description and dial
evidence.supports: Reports the date, tentative locality and spring-driven verge movement.

earliest_record.rationale: Earliest documented event for this scoped record, not a claim of worldwide priority.

research.note: Independent parent inspected the cited publisher, museum, BIPM or NIST/PTB passages. Dates retain their event scope; no global priority is inferred.

places.note: Antwerp or possibly Ghent, according to the catalogue.

caveats: The museum notes that the verge and balance may be replacements, so the surviving mechanism does not conclusively establish their 1571 configuration. The maker is identified only by initials; the exact city is uncertain and the fusee gut line is missing. No direct transmission to Huygens is established.
